input: Buy a standing mixer for holiday baking

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Standing mixers range from $50 to $700+. The budget determines which brands and models are even worth considering, completely changing the shortlist.

keyUnknowns.axis: scope / what baking tasks it must handle
keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Heavy doughs like bread or stollen demand a more powerful motor and dough-hook performance, while cookies and whipped cream are far less demanding — this shapes the required wattage and bowl capacity.

keyUnknowns.axis: people / household size and baking volume
keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Baking for a family of 4 vs. large holiday gatherings or gifting drives the bowl-size decision (4.5 qt vs. 7 qt) and how much continuous use the motor must withstand.
Counter space and cabinet clearance are hard physical limits — a large mixer may simply not fit, ruling out certain models regardless of other factors.
Some users have strong brand loyalty (e.g., KitchenAid) or care about specific features like a tilt-head vs. bowl-lift design, color, or attachments — this narrows the field quickly.

keyUnknowns.axis: logistics / where and how they want to buy
keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Buying in-store today vs. ordering online affects timeline, return policy, and whether holiday sales (Black Friday, etc.) should be factored into timing.

keyUnknowns.axis: success criteria / what done well looks like
keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: For some, success means the lowest price for a reliable machine; for others it means a long-term investment with expandable attachments — this sets the evaluation standard for the final choice.

questions.title: What is your budget for this mixer?
questions.description: Establish a firm or approximate price range (e.g., under $150, $150–$350, $350+) to determine which brands and models are realistic candidates.

questions.title: What types of dough or batters will you make most?
questions.description: Identify the heaviest or most demanding baking tasks (e.g., stiff bread dough, cookie dough, meringue) to determine the required motor power and attachments.

questions.title: How many people are you typically baking for?
questions.description: Understand batch sizes and baking frequency to recommend the right bowl capacity and motor durability.

questions.title: How much counter or cabinet space can you dedicate to it?
questions.description: Determine physical size constraints — height clearance under cabinets and available footprint — to rule out models that simply won't fit.

questions.title: Do you have a preferred brand or must-have feature?
questions.description: Capture any brand preferences (e.g., KitchenAid, Cuisinart) or design priorities (tilt-head vs. bowl-lift, color, specific attachments) to narrow the shortlist.

questions.title: Do you want to buy in-store or order it online?
questions.description: Clarify the preferred purchase channel to factor in shipping timelines, in-store availability, and whether upcoming holiday sales should influence timing.

questions.title: Is this a long-term investment or a budget-first purchase?
questions.description: Understand the user's overall priority — durability and expandability with attachments vs. getting a reliable machine at the lowest possible cost — to set the right evaluation standard.
